headline: Kenyan Women's Factory Slashes Sanitary Pad Costs in Half
meta_description: A women-led factory in Homa Bay, Kenya is producing affordable sanitary pads at 60% cheaper prices, with plans to donate to schools.
summary_short: A women-led factory in Homa Bay is revolutionizing menstrual health access by producing sanitary pads at a fraction of the cost—50 shillings per pack.
body:
A women-led factory in Homa Bay, Kenya is making sanitary pads available at up to 60% cheaper than conventional prices, with packs starting at just 50 shillings. The operation achieves remarkable efficiency, producing 200 pads per minute.

Beyond affordability, the factory has set its sights on a deeper goal: donating pads to schools to help girls remain in class. Missed school days due to lack of menstrual products remain a persistent barrier to education across East Africa, making this initiative both practical and transformative.

The venture demonstrates how locally-driven solutions can address fundamental health inequities while keeping costs accessible to the communities that need them most.
quick_facts: Women-led factory in Homa Bay, Kenya produces affordable sanitary pads
Pads cost 50 shillings per pack—up to 60% cheaper than market price
Plans to donate pads to schools to keep girls in class
